lessonRef.subject: mathematics
lessonRef.focus: comparing growth rates over the long run
lessonRef.title: Discussion or problem seminar: comparing growth rates over the long run

sections.title: Instructional examples
sections.directions: One approach is shown. There is at least one other that works.

steps: It is the multiplier per year.

sections.title: Guided practice
sections.directions: For each, name a second method before you solve it.

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (5, -26) and (9, -42). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.
A table of successive outputs reads 20, 60, 180, 540. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
choices: Exponential; successive outputs have a constant ratio of 3.
Linear; successive outputs differ by a constant 3.
Neither; the pattern does not repeat.
Quadratic; the second differences are constant.

items.prompt: A population of 2300 grows by 10% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 3 years, to the nearest whole number.

sections.title: Independent practice
sections.directions: Work on your own. Show the steps that produced each answer.

items.prompt: Quantity A grows by 106 units each year. Quantity B doubles or triples each year, with ratio 3, starting from a much smaller value. Which statement is true in the long run?
choices: B eventually exceeds A and stays ahead, however large A’s constant increase is.
A stays ahead permanently because 106 is larger than 3.
The two grow at the same eventual rate.
B exceeds A only if B starts larger than A.

items.prompt: An asset's value is modelled by V(t) = 3800(0.9)^t, with t in years. What does 3800 represent?
choices: the total value lost over the asset's life
the fraction of value retained each year, 0.9, meaning a 10% annual loss
the value of the asset when it was new, $3800
the number of years until the asset is worthless

items.prompt: A linear model passes through (5, -41) and (10, -86). Write it in the form f(x) = mx + b.

sections.title: Extension and challenge
sections.directions: Argue for one method over another. Say what makes it better, not just that it is.

items.prompt: A table of successive outputs reads 4, 20, 100, 500. Is the relationship linear or exponential, and why?
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.

items.prompt: A population of 2900 grows by 9% per year. Write the model P(t) and find the population after 7 years, to the nearest whole number.
items.responseExpectation: Give the result and the reasoning that produced it. Show enough work that someone else could check each step.
